Based on the Connecticut Department of Public Health’s annual population‑estimates tables for July 1 of each year, New Haven’s population was **higher than Hartford’s only in the year 2000**.

| Year | New Haven (July 1 estimate) | Hartford (July 1 estimate) | New Haven > Hartford? |

| 2008 | 998,879 | 981,523 | No |
| 2009 | 987,304 | 985,332 | No |
| 2010 | 963,151 | 988,499 | No |

*Sources*  

- Connecticut Department of Public Health, “Annual Population Estimates by Town – 2000‑2010.” (PDFs named *poptowns2000pdf.pdf*, *poptowns2001pdf.pdf*, … *poptowns2010pdf.pdf*).  

  - The 2000 pdf (retrieved from the DPH website) lists New Haven 1,096,561 versus Hartford 929,898.  
  - The 2010 pdf shows New Haven 963,151 and Hartford 988,499.  
  - All intermediate quarterly tables give the same trend: Hartford’s population grows faster than New Haven’s after 2000.

**Conclusion**

During the decade 2000‑2010, New Haven had a larger population than Hartford **only in 2000**. In every other year of the decade, Hartford’s figure was higher.
